title:
Solomon Islands Drops Its China Pact.
Pakistan Sends Its First Astronaut Up.
A US Jury Convicts Huawei.
subject: Solomon Islands Drops Its China Pact. Pakistan Sends Its First Astronaut Up. A US Jury Convicts Huawei.
preview_text: A Pacific pivot, a Pakistani in orbit, a Huawei verdict, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: Solomon Islands signs a treaty with Australia, Pakistan's first astronaut reaches China's space station and a US jury convicts Huawei.
contents_extra: Why the Houthis are hitting Saudi cities, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Solomon Islands Drops a China Pact for a Treaty With Australia
paragraphs: The BBC reports Solomon Islands signed a treaty with Australia in Canberra on Wednesday. It follows reports that Honiara told Beijing it would not renew a 2022 security pact. Prime Minister Matthew Wale said there were "ongoing discussions" with China. He said a non-disclosure agreement stopped him discussing the pact.

A joint statement from both prime ministers says the treaty reflects the choice of Australia as primary security partner. Australia will provide budget support and help fund free education, roads and renewable energy. Solomon Islanders will get longer visa stays. On Tuesday, China's foreign ministry neither confirmed nor denied the pact had ended, the BBC says.

stories.title: Pakistan's First Astronaut Joins a Chinese Space Mission
paragraphs: The BBC reports China launched Shenzhou-24 on Wednesday with Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali aboard. He is the first foreigner to join a Chinese crewed mission. The rocket lifted off at 00:18 GMT from the Gobi desert. Ali, a former fighter pilot, will return after a short stay. Two Chinese crewmates will spend six months aboard.

Reuters reports Ali became the first foreigner to board China's Tiangong space station. China is promoting Tiangong as a hub for international cooperation. The NASA-led International Space Station faces possible retirement by 2030. A Pakistani-built rover is also set to fly on a Chinese lunar mission around 2028, Reuters says.

photo.alt: A rocket launch in Florida, file photo

stories.title: A US Jury Convicts Huawei but Clears It of Racketeering
paragraphs: The BBC reports a Brooklyn jury found Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 counts on Tuesday. They included conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud and conspiracy to violate US sanctions. Jurors acquitted the Chinese firm of racketeering conspiracy. China's government criticised what it called US "suppression" of Chinese companies.

The Justice Department says Huawei lied to banks about its business in Iran. It says Huawei supplied surveillance cameras that helped Iranian authorities monitor protests. CNBC reports sentencing is scheduled for September 2027. Huawei called the remaining charges "without legal or factual merit" and said it would consider further legal action.

photo.alt: Huawei sign on an office building, file photo

deep_dive.title: Why the Houthis Are Taking Their War to Saudi Cities
paragraphs: CNBC reports a Houthi attack hit the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh on Tuesday, injuring 11 people. The injured included Saudi, Indian, Nepali and Egyptian nationals. It was the second attack on the tower in six days. A coalition spokesman called it a "cowardly terrorist attack" and said investigators were at the scene.

BBC Arabic reports the Houthis said on Wednesday they targeted the Ras Tanura refinery and a financial centre in Riyadh. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the refinery strike started fires. The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura. It reported falling debris but no injuries in an initial assessment.

The threats are widening. CNBC reports Saree warned on Wednesday that Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports would become targets if Riyadh attacks Hodeidah. The coalition had asked civilians to leave that Yemeni port on Nov. 20. The Houthis have also fired drones and missiles at Saudi airports, according to reports cited by CNBC.

Gulf economies are still absorbing the wider Iran war. CNBC reports the IMF now expects the UAE economy to grow 0.2% in 2026, revised from a 3.9% contraction forecast a month earlier. The UAE economy minister told CNBC the country is "very optimistic" about 7%-8% growth next year. Qatar and Pakistan condemned the Riyadh tower attack, BBC Arabic says.

trivia.question: On how many of 12 counts did a US jury find Huawei guilty?
trivia.explanation: The answer is 10. The BBC reports jurors cleared Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge.

South Africa's Ramaphosa wins a Phala Phala court fight, the BBC reports a panel's report was set aside.
Zimbabwe issues an arrest warrant for Robert Mugabe's son, the BBC reports he failed to appear in court on Tuesday.
Need to know: A Nigerian emir is suspended over sexual assault claims, the BBC reports a Polish tourist accused the 92-year-old Emir of Daura.
Leaked data suggest Russia has lost at least 490,334 soldiers, BBC Russian reports on Russian government statistics it analysed.
Israeli activists urge the release of a detained Palestinian student, the BBC reports Mahdi Tunsi is being held without charge.
Money & markets: Asian chip stocks tumble on Wednesday, CNBC reports Advantest plunged 12.94% as AI worries returned.
China's Xiamen Airlines agrees to buy 50 Boeing jets, CNBC reports a combined catalog price of about $7.4 billion.
Norse Atlantic shares plunge after a finance warning, CNBC reports they were last trading 76.8% lower on Wednesday.
Future frontiers: Europe's Hera probe reaches the asteroid Nasa hit in 2022, the BBC reports first images are set for release later on Wednesday.
A Saudi accused in an OpenAI bugging case wins release, CNBC reports a $1 million bond was set.
Taiwan's ruling party faces a wave of AI fakes, BBC Verify found a China-linked network made more than 500 fake videos.
The score: Arthur Rinderknech denies refusing a doping test, BBC Sport reports the ITIA confirmed he is under investigation.
Usman Khawaja says he is disappointed by Pat Cummins, BBC Sport reports on their row over the 2018 ball-tampering scandal.
Jannik Sinner has minor knee surgery, BBC Sport reports it comes seven weeks before the Australian Open.
Life & culture: Nollywood star Pete Edochie dies aged 79, the BBC reports his family said he died in Enugu.
A Cornwall Christmas market cancels all bookings after an AI backlash, the BBC reports visitors found a mostly empty hall.
EA will add an AI-generated John Motson voice to FC 27, the BBC reports his family gave permission.
